meta.title: Interpretable Integration of HDX-MS with Modern Protein Ensemble Generation
meta.author: Alexander Hussain
meta.arc: How can solution measurements distinguish structural explanations of protein dynamics, and how can that evidence guide the ensembles we generate?
meta.summary: A programme connecting validation, flexible ensemble inference, differentiable observables, and experimental guidance. Protein titration extends the same emphasis on interpretable, differentiable physical models into pH-dependent sequence objectives.
meta.narrative_basis: The programme-level narrative and conceptual connections are a synthesis of the repository sources, rather than a completed thesis argument.

journey.title: Ask what the data can distinguish
journey.text: HDX reports on exchange through an indirect, ensemble-level measurement. Multiple structural explanations can agree with those measurements.

journey.title: Validate the explanation
journey.text: Test unseen peptide information, quantify changes required during fitting, and compare candidate ensembles rather than relying on uptake error alone.

journey.title: Make inference flexible
journey.text: Use differentiable optimisation to adjust populations and prediction-model parameters, with composable losses, priors, and population benchmarks.
journey.takeaway: Separate model choices from structural evidence.

journey.title: Differentiate the observables
journey.text: Connect changing atomic coordinates to HDX, SAXS, and solvent-accessibility predictions so experimental objectives can influence structure updates.
journey.takeaway: Move from weight gradients to coordinate gradients.

journey.title: Guide generation and test its limits
journey.text: Couple ensemble fitting and coordinate gradients to Boltz sampling. Test identifiability, seeded maintenance, and creation of missing states as separate questions.
journey.takeaway: A mean fit is not population recovery.

journey.title: Extend differentiable physical modelling
journey.text: Model titration and charge on frozen structures under soft sequence identities, with gradients for pH-dependent bound/free objectives.

projects.name: ValDX
projects.tagline: Assess and rank candidate explanations of protein dynamics.
projects.question: How can we compare structural hypotheses when uptake agreement alone does not establish population accuracy?
projects.summary: A validation framework combining overlap-aware splitting, replicate-based uncertainty estimates, and Work Done diagnostics. It examines the effect of ensemble composition, clustering, fitting order, and kinetic misspecification.
projects.inputs: HDX uptake or residue protection factors; candidate structural ensembles from molecular dynamics and AlphaFold-derived sampling.
projects.outputs: Held-out predictions, uncertainty estimates, Work Done profiles, and comparative assessments of ensemble representativeness.
projects.boundary: Conclusions are comparative across supplied ensembles and the chosen forward model. Reweighting cannot add absent states; good uptake agreement does not validate exchange kinetics.
projects.next: Carry the post-review findings and their limits into Chapter 3, with explicit separation of predictive fit and structural inference.

claims.title: Prediction error is insufficient evidence of population accuracy
claims.text: The manuscript finds that conventional fitting error alone does not establish the accuracy of ensemble populations. Complementary diagnostics support comparison of candidate explanations.

claims.title: Validate unseen information, accounting for peptide overlap
claims.text: Sequence-based non-redundant and spatial splits remove overlapping training peptides; repeated splits assess sensitivity to the data partition.

claims.title: Work Done measures changes in model-predicted protection
claims.text: Shape, scale, and density describe different changes between prior and fitted protection profiles. Their interpretation remains conditional on the empirical forward model.

claims.title: The post-review study covers 22 ensembles across six proteins
claims.text: The abstract reports a multi-system evaluation, retention of performance at 10–20% of the parent ensemble through clustering, and smaller representations that aid interpretation.

claims.title: Fitting order changes population distortion under kinetic mismatch
claims.text: The synthetic benchmark reports that calibrating forward-model parameters before reweighting limits population distortion. Restored uptake agreement still does not establish population recovery or correct kinetics.

experiments.title: TeaA isolated validation
experiments.text: Open/closed reference conformations define a synthetic 40:60 target; bimodal and trimodal candidate ensembles probe population recovery and alternative support.

experiments.title: Multi-protein ensemble comparison
experiments.text: The post-review manuscript compares predictive agreement, Work Done, clustering, and optimisation protocols across candidate ensembles.

experiments.title: Imposed exchange-kinetic mismatch
experiments.text: A controlled departure from the EX2 fitting assumption tests whether model calibration and reweighting distort the generating populations.

modules.title: ValDX / ValidationDX.py
modules.text: Experiment orchestration around HDXer: predictions, split replicates, training, validation, and reweighting.

projects.name: jaxENT
projects.tagline: Fit populations and forward models in a flexible inverse-problem framework.
projects.question: How can ensemble weights, model parameters, and multiple experimental objectives be fitted efficiently and transparently?
projects.summary: A JAX/Optax platform for differentiable ensemble fitting with configurable parameter partitions and registered loss functions. Current examples explore synthetic recovery, prion-state comparisons, model regularisation, alpha-synuclein conditions, and joint HDX/SAXS fitting.
projects.inputs: Precomputed structural features; experimental observations; population priors; train/validation splits and observation covariance.
projects.outputs: Optimised frame weights and selected model parameters, predictions, optimisation histories, population scores, and model comparisons.
projects.boundary: The repository marks manuscript experiments as outdated. Its speedup, recovery-precision, and alpha-synuclein mechanistic claims are historical draft reports, not current validated conclusions in this map. Example workflows and implemented losses do not by themselves prove population recovery.
projects.next: Reconcile the manuscript with the current experiments and distinguish observation noise, forward-model discrepancy, and independently defined state-population targets.

claims.title: Weights and model parameters have separate trainable partitions
claims.text: Gradient masks and the optimiser expose frame-weight and forward-model parameter choices, supporting staged or joint optimisation.

claims.title: Inference uses configurable regularisation and observation losses
claims.text: The code contains entropy/divergence losses and Gaussian observation likelihoods. Physical Gaussian losses explicitly require observation covariance and reject trace-normalised covariance.

claims.title: Population scoring can be separated from predictive error
claims.text: State-population analysis includes explicit population estimates and strict Jensen–Shannon recovery scoring against supplied state targets.

claims.title: MoPrP examples explore a second regularisation axis
claims.text: A two-dimensional sweep varies MaxEnt strength and BV-parameter regularisation to examine the trade-off between data agreement, prior populations, and model-parameter robustness.

claims.title: Calmodulin examples compare HDX-only, SAXS-only, and joint fitting
claims.text: The example design uses a NeuralPlexer-derived ensemble and two CDZ conditions, with separate observation losses and cross-validation. It is evidence of the integration workflow, not a confirmed gain from combining modalities.

claims.title: Historical manuscript results need reconciliation
claims.text: The draft abstract reports performance and biological conclusions, while the thesis repository identifies its experiments as outdated. These statements are retained as historical context rather than promoted to current findings.

experiments.title: TeaA known-population inversion
experiments.text: Synthetic open/closed targets test recovery against a supplied 40:60 mixture rather than uptake agreement alone.

experiments.title: MoPrP conformational-state comparisons
experiments.text: Folded, PUF1, PUF2, and unfolded categories are assessed using structural features and literature-derived population references.

experiments.title: Alpha-synuclein across four solution conditions
experiments.text: Residue protection-factor fitting compares Tris-only, extracellular, intracellular, and lysosomal conditions; the documented PF-recovery score is not direct population ground truth.

experiments.title: Calmodulin with HDX and SAXS
experiments.text: Single-modality and combined fits compare two CDZ conditions and interrogate the balance between their losses.

modules.title: Optax optimiser and gradient masks
modules.text: Parameter partitions, learning-rate controls, and optimisation histories.

modules.title: Registered losses and population analysis
modules.text: Prior regularisation, Gaussian observation likelihoods, and independently supplied state targets.

projects.name: BioFeaturisers
projects.tagline: Turn atomic coordinates into differentiable biophysical predictions.
projects.question: How can structural observables carry gradients back to changing coordinates?
projects.summary: JAX kernels for HDX protection, SAXS profiles, and solvent-accessible surface area, with fixed-topology APIs and trajectory prediction. This supplies the coordinate-sensitive measurement layer used by experimental guidance.
projects.inputs: Atomic coordinates, fixed topology/features, prediction parameters, and optional ensemble weights.
projects.outputs: Contact-based protection profiles, HDX predictions, SAXS intensities, solvent accessibility, and coordinate gradients.
projects.boundary: A differentiable implementation is not a validation of the underlying physical approximation. The README records outstanding provenance and reference-benchmark work; test sources show checks that exist, not a newly executed test run.
projects.next: Benchmark prediction and gradient behaviour against independent references and document approximation and provenance limits.

claims.title: Fixed-topology APIs allow coordinates to change
claims.text: HDX and SAXS expose featurise_from_topology and predict_from_features paths; SASA supplies smooth, exact, and Gaussian-overlap modes with different topology behaviour.

claims.title: HDX kernels map coordinates to contact-based protection
claims.text: The forward kernel computes heavy-atom and backbone contact contributions and log protection factors under configurable empirical models.

claims.title: SAXS predictions support structures and trajectories
claims.text: The forward dispatch wraps FoXS-style single-structure and ensemble calculations with hydration and ensemble-weight options.

claims.title: Gradient checks are present in the source tree
claims.text: HDX gradient tests compare directional derivatives with finite differences. Their presence supports an implementation-audit trail; no package test pass is asserted from this map build.

experiments.title: Numerical and gradient verification
experiments.text: The package contains numerical fixtures and directional-gradient tests; independent physical validation remains a separate task.

modules.title: biofeaturisers.hdx
modules.text: Featurisation, coordinate-sensitive contact kernels, and prediction.

modules.title: biofeaturisers.saxs and .sasa
modules.text: Scattering and solvent-accessibility APIs for differentiable workflows.

projects.name: MaxENT-FK
projects.tagline: Guide Boltz ensembles while testing support and identifiability.
projects.question: Can experimental objectives improve structural populations during generation, beyond merely improving the mean observable?
projects.summary: A Chapter 5 workstream coupling Boltz sampling, BioFeaturisers coordinate gradients, and jaxENT fitting. Guidance modes include resampling, weighted gradients, and baseline controls, with explicit investigation of ensemble collapse and supplied-state support.
projects.inputs: Boltz particles, HDX targets, differentiable structural features, and guidance/regularisation schedules; synthetic controls may supply known conformers and moment targets.
projects.outputs: Guided structures, particle weights and lineage, observable diagnostics, and registered identifiability/maintenance decisions.
projects.boundary: Current governing V2 records do not establish HDX-only equilibrium population recovery or creation of absent basins. Oracle MD-derived variance targets and supplied open conformers must be identified as synthetic controls. Results here are reported by the handoff, not independently rerun or reanalysed.
projects.next: Audit which alternative structures reproduce open-like observables before treating better fit as a reason to tune the sampler or claim structural discovery.

claims.title: Guidance combines fitting, resampling, and coordinate updates
claims.text: The configuration separates FK resampling, weighted gradients, uniform-gradient guidance, and an unguided mode; the hook returns sampling weights and coordinate updates.

claims.title: Mean-observable losses cannot distinguish matched-mean collapse
claims.text: The V2 analysis explains that ensemble-mean MSE and the current residue-wise mean-curve transport assign the same loss to ensembles with the same weighted mean, even if their particle distributions differ.

claims.title: Supplied support permits recovery, but alternative support remains ambiguous
claims.text: The V2 report records recovery of the synthetic 40:60 mixture with a supplied two-state pool. Its overall verdict is observation_not_identifiable because a pool without open frames still fits below the registered missing-support failure threshold.

claims.title: Corrected maintenance experiment: null_or_harmful
claims.text: The governing true-lineage, five-seed experiment reports no structural maintenance improvement from the tested variance term and worse mean/variance observable errors than mean MSE alone; 0/5 seeds support the intervention.

claims.title: Identifiability, maintenance, and creation are different tests
claims.text: Recovering a mixture from supplied states, preserving seeded particle identities, and discovering an unsupported basin have different necessary conditions. Success in one does not establish the others.

experiments.title: TeaA supported-pool discriminator
experiments.text: Disjoint calibration/confirmation targets and missing-support controls separate conditional two-state recovery from structural ambiguity under alternative support.

experiments.title: TeaA true-lineage SDEdit maintenance
experiments.text: Matched unguided, mean-MSE, and mean-MSE-plus-variance conditions test the same seeded ensemble; the corrected five-seed verdict is null_or_harmful.

experiments.title: BPTI conformational-density case study
experiments.text: The example proposes comparing protection-factor-guided structures with NMR and MD references in disulfide torsion space. The README describes a workflow rather than an established positive result.

modules.title: maxent_fk.guidance.builder and .hook
modules.text: Connects BioFeaturisers and jaxENT to per-step sampling updates.

modules.title: maxent_fk.guidance.losses and .config
modules.text: Mean-observable, transport, and variance objectives with explicit baseline modes.

projects.name: jax-Ka
projects.tagline: Differentiate pH-dependent titration under soft sequence identities.
projects.question: Can interpretable titration and charge models supply useful sequence gradients for pH-dependent objectives?
projects.summary: The current implementation, jaxpropka, is a PROPKA-parameterised mean-field surrogate on frozen candidate geometry. It predicts charge, titration curves, and conditional pKa midpoints, and supplies a bound/free selectivity objective.
projects.inputs: Prepared protein structures and frozen candidate geometry, residue-wise amino-acid probabilities, pH grids, and model settings.
projects.outputs: Conditional protonation, residue/chain/total charge, pKa midpoints, sequence gradients, and explicit convergence diagnostics.
projects.boundary: This is not a numerically faithful PROPKA port or an experimentally calibrated pKa predictor. Frozen geometry, mean-field coupling, and solver-branch behaviour limit interpretation. CPU numerical qualification does not establish a unique equilibrium, experimental accuracy, or accelerator performance.
projects.next: Evaluate native and mutant predictions against independent data, validate gradient directions with discrete rescoring, and retain convergence and branch audits in design objectives.

claims.title: The model is a frozen-geometry mean-field surrogate
claims.text: The README explicitly distinguishes the model from PROPKA's coupled determinant algorithm; geometry is prepared outside the JIT sequence readouts.

claims.title: Charge, titration curves, and conditional midpoints are exposed
claims.text: Readouts retain separate conditional identity channels and numerical diagnostics for convergence, bracketing, and root validity.

claims.title: Bound/free objectives differentiate binder sequence probabilities
claims.text: The selectivity objective holds structure and target identities fixed, relates bound and isolated environments, and differentiates the soft binder sequence.

claims.title: Numerical and scientific validation remain distinct
claims.text: The documentation reports analytic and directional-gradient checks and an opt-in CPU design preset that passed numerical gates. It also states that experimental calibration and broader scientific acceptance remain open.

experiments.title: Analytic, gradient, and external-reference checks
experiments.text: The validation inventory reports independent-site limits, directional finite differences, topology handling, and PROPKA discrepancy tests; these are documented checks rather than experiments rerun for this map.

experiments.title: CPU design-preset qualification
experiments.text: The documentation reports numerical promotion across protein–protein interfaces with explicit failed/nonqualifying samples and caller-controlled branch audits.

modules.title: jaxpropka.model
modules.text: Sequence-dependent local terms, coupled titration solves, and midpoint readouts.

modules.title: jaxpropka.selectivity
modules.text: Bound/free charge objectives and gradients with fixed-environment checks.

connections.title: Validation motivates flexible inference
connections.text: ValDX exposes the dependence of structural conclusions on splitting, diagnostics, and fitting order. jaxENT provides a flexible platform to investigate those choices; this is the research narrative, not a software-import dependency.

connections.title: The same validation question recurs in generation
connections.text: Both workstreams distinguish predictive agreement from a correct structural population. Guidance extends the challenge to particle support, lineage, and missing basins.

connections.title: Ensemble fitting inside guidance
connections.text: MaxENT-FK lists jax-ent as a dependency and imports its optimisation and dataset interfaces when constructing guidance.

connections.title: Coordinate-sensitive observables supply guidance gradients
connections.text: MaxENT-FK imports BioFeaturisers HDX configuration and features; the guidance hook connects predicted protection/uptake losses to coordinate updates.

connections.title: Complementary differentiable layers
connections.text: jaxENT fits weights and model parameters around structural features. BioFeaturisers makes the feature/observable calculations responsive to changing coordinates. The map does not assert a direct package dependency between them.

connections.title: Shared emphasis on differentiable physical models
connections.text: Coordinate-sensitive observables and sequence-sensitive titration share a methodological emphasis on gradients, interpretable approximations, and separate numerical/scientific checks. No HDX-to-pKa coupling is established in the cited code.

observations.title: The thesis is an outline, not a completed results document
observations.text: Chapters 1–2 provide the agreed introduction/background headings. The project chapters remain placeholders, so scientific content is drawn from the project repositories and manuscripts.

observations.title: Current code and historical manuscripts have different authority
observations.text: The jaxENT manuscript is labelled outdated in the root README. Implemented capabilities, example designs, and historical manuscript conclusions are presented separately.

observations.title: Guidance has a superseding interpretation
observations.text: The V2 handoff supersedes earlier Stage 3 claims. Supported-pool ambiguity and the corrected null_or_harmful maintenance verdict govern this map.

observations.title: jax-Ka has advanced beyond the brief root status label
observations.text: The project README says preliminary training, while the current code documentation records an implemented surrogate and numerical qualification. Scientific calibration is still explicitly open.
